source: NCERT Class XI, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 1), Ch. 1 (Prehistoric Rock Paintings).

sections.heading: 1. Prehistoric Art — Overview
points: Prehistoric people painted on **cave/rock walls** (rock art); the earliest surviving art in India.
Periods: **Upper Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, and Chalcolithic**; the richest phase is the **Mesolithic**.
Purpose: possibly ritual/magic, record of life, or decoration; paintings depict **hunting, dancing, animals and daily life**.

sections.heading: 2. Major Sites
points: **Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh)** — the most important site; a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**; hundreds of painted rock shelters discovered by **V.S. Wakankar**.
Other sites: **Lakhudiyar (Uttarakhand), Kupgallu (Telangana), Piklihal and Tekkalkota (Karnataka)**.
Bhimbetka paintings span from the Palaeolithic to historic times.

sections.heading: 3. Themes, Colours and Style
points: **Themes:** animals (bison, tigers, elephants, deer), **hunting scenes**, dancing, food gathering, riding — human and animal figures.
**Colours (natural mineral pigments):** **red (haematite/geru), white, green, yellow**; the most common were **red and white**.
Figures are often shown in a lively, dynamic manner; animals drawn with skill; **X-ray style** and superimposition of paintings seen.

sections.heading: 4. Significance
points: These paintings reveal the **life, beliefs and environment** of early humans.
They show continuity — layers of paintings from different periods at the same site.
They are the beginning of the Indian artistic tradition.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Bhimbetka (MP) = most important prehistoric rock art site (UNESCO); discovered by V.S. Wakankar.
Richest phase of rock paintings = Mesolithic.
Common colours = red (haematite/geru) and white.
Themes = hunting, animals, dancing, daily life.
Lakhudiyar (Uttarakhand), Kupgallu (Telangana) = other sites.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Bhimbetka** is in **Madhya Pradesh** and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
It was discovered/studied by **V.S. Wakankar**.
The **Mesolithic** period has the richest rock paintings.
The most common pigment colours were **red and white** (from minerals).
